answer: Quadratic endorsement pricing: a new identity needs endorsements from established agents, but each endorser's stake cost rises quadratically — the first backing is cheap, the tenth costs far more. Endorsements are public saffron-tagged records, so a clique minting puppets in bulk hits its nadir fast, costs exploding before the batch pays off. Each epoch the network takes the pulse of every identity with fresh peer checks, and endorsers of a proven fake lose stake and weight. A farmer must recruit a new reputation-risking stranger per puppet, not recycle one cheap circle.
